Needs changes before merge.

The separate source evaluation gives correct user line numbers. The new preview samples post through both specified milling posts. The change adds no dependency.

This is a safety-tier review. I reviewed the new commit and the inherited changes from #468. I read both added thread goldens line by line. The sandbox commit changes no golden files.

Local validation:

- `cargo test -p camcraft-post --no-run`: passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: 562 passed, 0 failed. This includes all 10 sandbox tests and all 3 preview tests.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test turning_thread_dips`: 9 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test lathe_post_thread_dips --test lathe_post_inch`: 12 passed, 0 failed. Both thread goldens passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`, from `crates/ui`: 815 passed, 6 ignored, 0 failed. No ignored pixel tests ran.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed for `camcraft-post`, `camcraft-cl`, `camcraft-motion`, `camcraft-app`, and `camcraft-ui` (selected with `-p`).
- Mutation 1: I removed the Rust output-length guard. The run-boundary test failed with exit 101 because the post accepted 100,001 lines.
- Mutation 2: I removed the output-length check from `drain`. The before-drain test failed with exit 101 because the drain accepted 100,001 items.
- After restoration, all 10 sandbox tests passed. All temporary test changes were removed.
- The added regression check for a caught output-limit error failed on the unchanged implementation: `accepted truncated program with 100000 lines`.

All commands ran locally in the review worktree. No GitHub runner was used.

Requested before merge:

1. `crates/post/src/post/js_host.rs:11` and `crates/post/src/post/js.rs:343`: Make an output-limit failure persist after a script catches the exception. `_emitLine` throws before it adds line 100,001. A script can catch that error. The Rust check then accepts the remaining 100,000 lines. I reproduced a successful post with a truncated program and no warning. This violates the rule that incomplete output must be refused. Add a test that catches the error in the script and still requires the post to fail. This script reproduces the defect:

   ```javascript
   function onOpen() {
     try {
       for (var i = 0; i < 100001; i++) writeBlock('G01 X1');
     } catch (e) {}
   }
   ```

2. `crates/ui/src/egui_app/thread_infeed_page.rs:57`: Add before/after screenshots to this PR body for the added thread controls. The current diff against `main` includes these UI changes, but this PR body has no screenshots. #468 has screenshots. Include the required evidence here, or remove the inherited UI diff when the parent merges. Store any new screenshots only on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch.

Merge status: The trial merge with `upstream/main` at `780b0a25a40606dc3cc96f56ab0b2c8ecb1093e6` failed in `crates/app/src/operation/params.rs`. I aborted the merge and tested the unchanged PR head. These results do not prove the merged tree. Refresh the branch at merge time, as the repository rules require. No code conflict was resolved for this review.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed: none. Stopped at the required merge-conflict safety boundary. No fixes or commits were pushed.

The conflict is in `crates/app/src/operation/params.rs`, in `OpParams::stamp_with`. The PR adds chip-break-dip hashing to the Threading arm: tag `0xD6` and interval, height and length. Main moves that arm into `params/turning.rs::stamp_turning` and replaces the inline arms with dispatch calls. This is a refactor that moved code the PR edits. Resolving it requires reconciling the logic across that move. The author-side instructions require stopping for this kind of hunk.

I aborted the merge. The head remains `236d40d640fb1470471fa04ba1e0771d2a0bb51e`. No tests, mutations, quick gate or clippy ran.

Both findings remain open: persistent refusal after a caught output-limit exception, and before/after thread-control screenshots in this PR body. Please resolve the conflicting hunk before continuing the fixes and requesting re-review.

Addressed both review findings from `IC_kwDOVVonwM8AAAABm68S0w` on new head `df155962d7f8c2623a7988f5d2d21dd83ad1f313`:

1. Persistent output-limit refusal (`crates/post/src/post/js_host.rs`, `crates/post/src/post/js.rs`): `_emitLine` now latches a read-only `_outputLimitExceeded` getter before throwing. `Script::load`, `Script::call`, and `Script::out_len` (used by `drain`) check and latch `output_limit_exceeded` in Rust, so catching the exception or resetting globals still refuses the post. Pinned by `caught_output_limit_error_is_still_refused` in `crates/post/tests/script_sandbox.rs` (mutation-checked: reverted fix failed RED, restored fix passed GREEN).
2. Thread-control screenshots (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/thread_infeed_page.rs`): Copied the inherited before/after Threading Passes tab renders from #468 (`39632f647`; `thread_infeed_page.rs` is unchanged on this branch) to the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch (`ebc3d596f234b848ed2392c7cdc180c85afaa918`, under `2115/`). Updating the PR body failed from this host (`gh pr edit` in `gh 2.46.0` hits GitHub's `repository.pullRequest.projectCards` GraphQL deprecation error, and `gh api -X PATCH` is disallowed by local policy), so the renders are attached below until the PR body is updated (or the inherited UI diff drops after #468 merges):

Before (`origin/main`):

![Threading Passes tab before](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/ebc3d596f234b848ed2392c7cdc180c85afaa918/2115/before.png?raw=true)

After (with #468):

![Threading Passes tab after](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/ebc3d596f234b848ed2392c7cdc180c85afaa918/2115/after.png?raw=true)

Gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`, falling back to `batch` due to inherited `crates/cl/src/cl/thread.rs` diff from #468; unresolved #468 base conflict in `crates/app/src/operation/params.rs` left for merge-time refresh):
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test script_sandbox`: 11 passed, 0 failed.
- 9 of 10 gate steps passed (`geometry`, `kernel`, `cl`, `tools`, `post`, `sim`, `motion`, `ui`, and `clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` on all 8 workspace crates). `camcraft-app` failed only on the two documented #468 base issues (`docs_troubleshooting::troubleshooting_messages_still_exist_in_the_sources`, `operations::threaded_batch_matches_the_serial_loop_bit_for_bit`).

Ready for a re-review.

Needs changes before merge.

The output-limit fix meets the earlier code request. A caught output-limit exception now causes a persistent refusal. The regression test also covers top-level output and attempts to reset the globals.

This is a safety-tier review. The inherited changes from #468 affect posted G-code and thread safety checks. I read both added thread goldens line by line. The metric and inch goldens passed. The sandbox changes do not change a golden file.

Local results:

- `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-post --no-run`: passed.
- `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-post`: 563 passed, no failures. This includes 11 sandbox tests and 3 preview tests.
- `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-motion --test turning_thread_dips`: 9 passed, no failures.
- `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-app --test lathe_post_thread_dips --test lathe_post_inch --test turning_thread_infeed --test lathe_post_g76_schedule`: 24 passed, no failures.
- `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-ui --lib`, from `crates/ui`: 815 passed, 6 ignored, no failures. No ignored pixel tests ran.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- The quick-gate dry run selected the batch tier because the inherited diff changes `crates/cl`. I ran the touched suites above. I did not run the full batch tier or a wasm build.

I repeated two mutations locally:

1. I removed the Rust output-length guard. `direct_output_buffer_writes_are_refused_at_run_boundary` failed with exit 101. The post accepted 100,001 lines.
2. I restored that guard and removed the `drain` output-length check. `direct_output_buffer_writes_are_refused_before_drain` failed with exit 101. The drain accepted 100,001 items.

After restoration, all 11 sandbox tests passed. The review worktree has no source changes.

Requested before merge:

1. `crates/ui/src/egui_app/thread_infeed_page.rs:57`: Put the before/after screenshots in this PR body. The added thread controls remain in this PR's diff. The latest author comment links both images, but the body has neither image. Copy those links into the body, or remove the inherited UI diff after #468 merges. Keep the images on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch. Do not commit them to the PR branch.

Merge status: The trial merge with `upstream/main` at `a49322b9c0c049bd0b3b2d1dea855de6087ac64b` failed in `crates/app/src/operation/params.rs`. Main moved the hashing code that this PR changes. I aborted the merge and tested the unchanged PR head. These results do not prove the merged tree. Refresh the branch at merge time under the repository rules. I did not resolve the code conflict.

All commands ran locally in `.claude/worktrees/review-2115`. No GitHub runner was used. Keep `needs-rework` and `conflicts`. Keep the PR as a draft.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed: the latest review's screenshot finding. The PR body now includes both before/after Threading Passes tab image links from the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` commit `ebc3d596f234b848ed2392c7cdc180c85afaa918`. I read the body back through the API and verified both links. No images or evidence were committed to the PR branch. This body-only change needs no source test or mutation.

Stopped at the required merge-conflict boundary. Merging `upstream/main` (`dab6498ae`) conflicts in `crates/app/src/operation/params.rs`, in `OpParams::stamp_with`. This PR adds chip-break-dip hashing to the Threading arm: tag `0xD6`, interval, height and length. Main moves that arm to `params/turning.rs::stamp_turning` and replaces the inline arms with dispatch calls. Reconciling the moved logic meets the explicit stop condition. I aborted the merge and verified a clean worktree.

Head remains `df155962d7f8c2623a7988f5d2d21dd83ad1f313`. No commit or push was needed for the body update. Quick gate and clippy were not run because the required merge stopped. The PR remains a draft and its labels are unchanged.

Please re-review the screenshot finding on this unchanged head. The merge conflict remains unresolved.
